subject: Research digest: Retrieval Augmented Generation – 10 new paper(s)

ai_overview.overview: These papers show RAG moving from proof-of-concept demos toward engineering-first, trust-oriented systems that prioritize faithfulness, attribution, and domain adaptivity. Key contributions include iterative, agentic evidence refinement (FAIR-RAG), context-aware gating and calibration mechanisms to avoid irrelevant or misleading context, and large-scale efforts to standardize evaluation and deployment practices (TREC 2025, RAGEv, and a comprehensive taxonomy). Work spans cross-cutting concerns: stronger benchmarks and metrics, reproducibility challenges with closed LLMs, and practical architectures for heterogeneous data and high-stakes domains.
trends: Faithfulness and attribution-first RAG (iterative evidence auditing and grounding)
Benchmarking and evaluation maturation (task-specific benchmarks, multi-dimensional metrics, and shared tracks)
Modular, agentic, and multi-agent architectures for heterogeneous and private data
recommended_first: FAIR-RAG: Faithful Adaptive Iterative Refinement for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Engineering the RAG Stack: A Comprehensive Review of the Architecture and Trust Frameworks for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
Overview of the TREC 2025 Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) Track
open_questions: How can we standardize attribution and faithfulness metrics that generalize across domains and generation styles?
What are cost- and latency-efficient strategies to guarantee evidence completeness (multi-hop) without excessive retrieval/query cycles?
How can reproducibility be ensured when core LLM components are closed-source or rapidly changing?
